recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not restore the older blanket conformance list; the current in-band/out-of-band wording is the better current-spec expression of the FHIR-31946 requirement after later approved R6 work.
issue_request: FHIR-31946 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Subscription and asked how servers declare Subscription support. Its resolution imported the R4 Backport requirements: support the Subscription resource for read/write, support Subscription $status, support SubscriptionTopic for read/search, support at least one channel type and one payload type, and document support that cannot be expressed in CapabilityStatement out of band.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by commit d35d9e104bc474133430758027a6da4ad7b1b667, which added Conformance and Discovery sections to source/subscriptions.html. That page is referenced by current source navigation, and Subscription, SubscriptionStatus, and SubscriptionTopic are active resources in source/fhir.ini.
additional_context: FHIR-31459 is the matching published R4 Backport issue that FHIR-31946 directed core to follow. Later FHIR-46495 intentionally split Subscription conformance into in-band and out-of-band management styles, relaxing some resource and operation requirements for out-of-band management while preserving the in-band requirements plus channel, payload, and discovery guidance. Later FHIR-47288 resolved no-change on a request to force out-of-band subscriptions to follow the in-band rules, supporting the current split.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/subscriptions.html already states the conformance requirements and discovery limitation, and the differences from the original single-list wording are explained by later applied decisions rather than by incomplete application.
